fact: The World Bank report states the National Payments Systems Act, 2022 has been enacted and repealed the earlier Payment Systems Act, 2009.

The World Bank report states the Bank of Sierra Leone's Guidelines for E-money are completed and gazetted, as are guidelines on money remittance business, e-KYC guidelines and directives for the switch; report dated 2023-06-23, which is used as the date as no other is given.
The National Payment Systems Act, 2022 (Act 8 of 2022), assented to 2 June 2022 and published in Gazette 43, commenced on 23 June 2022 and repealed the Payments Systems Act 2009.

The National Payment Systems Act, 2022 (s.6) bars any person from providing payment services or operating a system without a Bank of Sierra Leone licence and sets e-money issuer conditions, while s.8 exempts only banks and financial institutions from needing a new licence; s.5 seats mobile money operators and the Fintech Association on the National Payment System Committee. Date is the Act's commencement.

Bank of Sierra Leone National Switch Directives issued December 2024 require all commercial banks and mobile money operators to process instant, card and POS transactions through the national switch SaPS from 1 April 2025.
